cultural.vision_reason: This is a distinctive Sámi ládjogahpir (horn cap), a well-documented traditional women's headdress from Norway with its characteristic curved horn shape, red wool, and brocaded trim bands, clearly matching the claimed ethnicity and category.

physical.title: cap; hat
physical.summary: A woman's hat, or cap (ládjogahpir'), with a high extension on the crown (a), its shape held in place with a hollow piece of carved wood (b).  Made of red wool woven cloth, commercially made.  Fitted across the forehead, with flaps either side, secured under the chin with yellow plaited wool cord and a strip of printed cloth.  Blue wool cloth stitched to section framing face (decorated with two lines of cream cotton rickrack) and back of neck.  Above front is a wide piece of polychrome brocaded silk (?) cloth, with another line of cream rickrack above.  Two strips of blue and yellow cloth stitched in a vertical line to hat extension.
